ticket.title: A suite should declare its members, so membership can be resolved without a hardcoded roster
ticket.description:
Reaching the canonical ledger from inside a member repository needs the suite to DECLARE its members. Layout alone cannot answer it: a member carries its own .gaugeblock (an index, a stub, a docs config) and so looks exactly like a suite of one, and a suite root is itself a git repository containing members, which is indistinguishable from a repository containing a nested checkout.

Two candidate answers, both rejected as written:
  * WorkspaceTopology::expected_members is a hardcoded roster. It answers for this suite and for no other, and it makes Membership untestable under fixture names.
  * A git-boundary rule with "nearest candidate wins" cannot separate member-of-suite from nested-checkout-of-repo, because both have the store above the caller's own repository root.

The declaration should live in .gaugeblock/config.toml, e.g. [suite] members = [...], read through SuiteConfig, with absence meaning "no members" - the safe direction, since a repository that cannot prove it belongs somewhere keeps its own ledger.

Once that exists, SP-29's ledger-from-anywhere step is a two-line change in StorypoleStore::open, which already routes through store_locate and already prefers a ledger over a stub.

verification_receipt.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo nextest run --workspace && miter audit --path . --threshold 250 --paths && chalkline docs check -d .
